sara: FYI — while investigating a prod perf regression we found kpick sampling + KV cache hit ratio cause different kernel choices between A100-SXM and A100-PCIE. Sharing quick notes and logs below.

kevin: uhoh. what sample rate are we using? :thinking:

sara: prod uses KPICK_SAMPLING=0.01 (default). Increasing to 0.1 locally exposed much more variance. simple repro: sweep seq_len 64..512, batch=8, vary kv-hit-prob.

liam: can you paste a log snippet so we can see the pick reasons?

sara: sure — here's an example from the run where the flip happens (seq_len=256, kv_hit_prob=0.8):
```
[kpick] ts=1748001235 request_id=rid-42 arch=a100_sxm seq_len=256 batch=8 kv_prefix_ratio=0.82 chosen=GEMM_F16_FAST reason=cost_model score=-12.34 sample_id=7
[kpick] ts=1748001236 request_id=rid-43 arch=a100_pcie seq_len=256 batch=8 kv_prefix_ratio=0.82 chosen=GEMM_INT8_TILED reason=latency_est score=-11.90 sample_id=7
[serve] kv_cache_hit=0.81 latency_ms=21.4 tokens=256
```
Observation: same sample_id (sampling hit), but cost model & arch heuristics prefer different kernels depending on arch and on whether kv_prefix_ratio > ~0.6.

kevin: looks like the cost model is overweighting kv_prefix_ratio for SXM vs PCIE or the kernel cost tables differ between arch tags. also sampling noise (sample_id) means we see nondeterministic switches.

anika: we should add structured telemetry fields so we can slice these quickly in Console dashboards. proposed KPICK fields: kpick.kernel, kpick.reason, kpick.score, kpick.sample_rate, kpick.kv_prefix_ratio, kpick.seq_bucket, kpick.arch_tag, kpick.cache_mode. also add a trace id for sample_id.

eng-bot: flag deployed: KPICK_DEBUG_LOG=trace to canary pool. Notifying @sara @kevin.

sara: thanks. I'll run a batch sweep and upload flamegraphs + cost-model heatmaps to the ticket. Repro script I'm using: `./tools/kpick_sweep.sh --seqs 64 128 256 512 --batches 1 8 16 --kv-hit-probs 0 0.5 0.9 --sample-rate 0.01 0.1`

kevin: :thumbsup: two followups — (1) add a deterministic fallback when sample variance causes >5% change in chosen kernel distribution for same workload; (2) normalize kv_prefix_ratio influence across arch tags or make it a tunable weight exposed via env flag KPICK_KV_WEIGHT.

liam: filed PERF-9876 with logs and initial flamegraphs, assigning to eng-runtime. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PERF-9876

sara: I'll update the ticket with the canary results in ~1h. TL;DR: sampling + kv interactions expose arch-sensitive kernel choices; need better telemetry and a short-term deterministic guard to avoid production regressions.
